note: Frozen evaluation design for the initial family release. No isolated live executor or unseen external holdout was available in this authoring run.

release_holdout.reason: The public development cases are visible to the author. A genuine release holdout must be controlled outside the optimizing context.

evals.name: multi-scale-state-design
evals.prompt: Design a reusable model for predicting customer renewal from interaction events collected over time.
evals.fixtures: Prompt-only scenario with no private customer data or live system access.
evals.output_contract: A time-aware model specification that separates event aggregation, probability estimation, and the renewal decision.
evals.failure_consequence: A leaky or objective-free model could produce a confident but unusable renewal intervention.

expectations.text: Response defines an explicit target, forecast horizon, and as-of timestamp.
Response includes the event-to-state aggregation ladder.
Response names a time-aware split or as-of leakage control.
Response separates the probability forecast from the decision objective and constraints.

evals.name: feature-compression-test
evals.prompt: I have 240 correlated features and want to know whether fewer than 200 explain most of the useful signal.
evals.fixtures: Prompt-only scenario with a supplied feature count but no outcome table.
evals.output_contract: A nested feature-tier experiment with baseline, out-of-sample metrics, and leakage-aware feature inventory.
evals.failure_consequence: A feature-count slogan could be mistaken for validated compression or explanatory power.

expectations.text: Response proposes nested feature tiers including 10, 30, 60, 120, and 200 when supported.
Response requires comparison with a simple baseline using out-of-sample metrics.
Response distinguishes explainable signal from raw winner-prediction accuracy or certainty.
Response requires a feature inventory containing provenance, grain, cadence, and leakage risk.

evals.name: intervention-aware-allocation
evals.prompt: Choose where to spend a limited budget when historical performance is correlated with customer quality and assigned opportunity difficulty.
evals.fixtures: Prompt-only scenario with confounding and opportunity-assignment language but no private records.
evals.output_contract: A bias-aware allocation specification with objective, constraints, and causal validation plan.
evals.failure_consequence: The system could reward selection bias or allocate scarce resources to the easiest opportunities.

expectations.text: Response checks selection bias, confounding, and opportunity assignment.
Response asks what would have happened without the proposed action.
Response states an explicit objective function with cost or capacity constraints.
Response recommends an experiment, holdout, or clearly labeled observational design when causal impact is claimed.

evals.name: reproducible-calculation
evals.prompt: Show how a small event history becomes a weighted state, probability, calibration score, and expected-value comparison.
evals.output_contract: A plain-language calculation that defines symbols, reports intermediate values, and preserves the distinction between forecast and decision.
evals.failure_consequence: A reader could mistake an unexplained number or arithmetic example for a validated forecast.

expectations.text: Response defines the weighted mean, logistic probability, Brier score, and expected-value calculations.
Response shows at least one intermediate calculation rather than only a final ranking.
Response expands technical terms or points to the glossary for a non-specialist reader.
Response states that a synthetic calculation does not establish live predictive performance.
